errors.claim: Sustainable marketing is now a business imperative rather than a CSR add-on.
errors.searches: business imperative; CSR add-on; corporate social responsibility; sustainable marketing
errors.source_check: The source explicitly calls sustainability a business imperative and later contrasts traditional shareholder primacy with CSR/ESG accountability, but it does not characterise CSR as an add-on or frame sustainable marketing with that exact opposition.

errors.claim: Customer equity is the cumulative profit a company earns from current and potential customers.
errors.searches: customer equity; cumulative profit; potential profits; current and potential customers
errors.source_check: The source repeatedly defines customer equity as the total potential profits from current and potential customers. 'Cumulative profit' changes the source's prospective wording.

errors.claim: The buying centre has up to seven roles: initiator, influencer, gatekeeper, buyer, decider, and user.
errors.searches: buying center roles; seven roles; initiator influencer gatekeeper buyer decider user; business and technical influencers
errors.source_check: The source identifies six roles: initiator, influencer, gatekeeper, buyer, decider, and user. Business and technical are two categories within the influencer role, not separate buying-centre roles.

errors.claim: Coca-Cola uses the same brand, name, scriptural cursive, and red/white presentation worldwide.
errors.searches: scriptural cursive; iconic cursive; Coca-Cola white on red; standardized global marketing strategy
errors.source_check: The source says Coca-Cola's 'iconic cursive writing in white on red background' is seen worldwide. 'Scriptural cursive' is not the source's description and appears to be a wording error.

errors.claim: The United States will become a 'plurality nation' by the mid-2040s, meaning no group will have a sizeable majority.
errors.searches: plurality nation; mid-2040s; majority-minority population shift; no group sizeable majority; by 2050
errors.source_check: The source predicts a majority-minority shift by the mid-2040s, but separately says the country will become a 'plurality nation' by 2050, when no group has a sizeable majority. The reference conflates the two formulations and dates.

errors.claim: The Hispanic population is the fastest-growing US multicultural group.
errors.searches: Hispanic fastest-growing; one of the fastest-growing groups; 59 percent population growth; Asian fastest population growth
errors.source_check: The source calls the Hispanic population 'one of the fastest-growing groups.' It says the combined Asian classifications experienced the fastest population growth among multicultural segments between 2000 and 2019. Dropping 'one of' overstates the Hispanic claim.

errors.claim: Facebook had 2.9 billion monthly active users and $117.92 billion in 2020 revenue.
errors.searches: Facebook 117.92 billion; 2020 revenue; Facebook revenue and usage statistics; 2.9 billion monthly active users
errors.source_check: The Facebook passage gives 2.9 billion monthly active users and $117.92 billion in revenue but supplies no year for that revenue figure. No targeted source search supports the added '2020' qualifier.

errors.searches: eight store-retailer types; Types of Retailers; Table 18.1; specialty store; warehouse club; factory outlet
errors.source_check: Table 18.1 enumerates ten store-retailer types: specialty, department, supermarket, superstore, convenience, category killer, discount, off-price, factory outlet, and warehouse club.

errors.claim: Facebook monthly active users: 2.9 billion; $117.92 billion 2020 revenue.
errors.searches: Facebook 117.92 billion; 2020 revenue; 2.9 billion monthly active users; Facebook Revenue and Usage Statistics 2022
errors.source_check: This key-statistics row repeats the unsupported year qualifier. The source provides the user count and revenue amount but does not identify the revenue as 2020 revenue.

errors.claim: Hofstede's cultural dimensions are cited approvingly as the dominant frame for cross-cultural marketing analysis.
errors.searches: Hofstede dominant frame; particularly useful in assessing culture; cultural dimensions; Values and Attitudes
errors.source_check: The source calls Hofstede's model 'particularly useful' and applies it in Chapters 5 and 8, but it does not call the model dominant. 'Dominant frame' is a modest overstatement of the source's evaluative language.
